blocks.text: Fixed asset and lease accounting policy
HANGS Construction Services LLC
Status: approved by the board, effective July 1, 2025
1. What is capitalized
1.1 Equipment with a cost of $5,000.00 or more and a life of more than one year is capitalized at its full cost: price, delivery, assembly and setup.
1.2 Repairs and maintenance, including rebuilds of an existing asset’s parts that keep it working, are expensed when incurred.
1.3 Every purchase of $25,000.00 or more needs a capital expenditure request approved by the president before the order is placed.
2. Depreciation
2.1 Straight-line by month on cost less salvage, rounded to the cent, a full month in the month placed in service and none in the month of disposal; the last month takes what is left.
2.2 Lives and salvage by class (used equipment takes its class life unless the equipment manager documents a shorter one):
Class: Heavy earthmoving equipment; life 120 months; salvage 20% of cost
Class: Cranes and crane attachments; life 240 months; salvage 20% of cost
Class: Concrete pump trucks; life 120 months; salvage 15% of cost
Class: Trucks and trailers; life 96 months; salvage 15% of cost
Class: Site office units; life 180 months; salvage 0% of cost
Class: Loaders, telehandlers and skid steers; life 84 months; salvage 10% of cost
Class: Survey and layout equipment; life 60 months; salvage 0% of cost
2.3 A disposal removes the asset’s cost and accumulated depreciation; the difference from the proceeds is a gain or loss in equipment costs.
3. Leases
3.1 Every agreement for equipment or space is read under ASC 842: a lease is a contract for the right to control an identified asset for a period.
3.2 Leases of 12 months or less with no purchase option HGC is reasonably certain to exercise are short-term: expensed, not recognized.
3.3 Other leases are recognized at the present value of the payments, discounted at the incremental borrowing rate, the equipment term loan’s 7.10%.
Demonstration document. Every name and figure is invented.

The register agrees with the books: cost $7,120,000.00 (account 1550), accumulated depreciation $2,465,500.00 (account 1590) and the year’s depreciation $424,700.00 (account 6600). Net equipment is $4,654,500.00.

trail.what: Plan the Area
trail.result: Materiality $340,000.00 · the register agrees with accounts 1550, 1590 and 6600

trail.what: Roll cost and accumulated depreciation forward, asset by asset
trail.result: Cost: $5,790,100.00 at June 30, 2025, plus $1,432,500.00 of additions, less $102,600.00 scrapped, is $7,120,000.00. Accumulated depreciation: $1,963,400.00, plus $424,700.00 of depreciation, less $102,600.00 on the scrapped trailers, plus $180,000.00 of “other entries”, is $2,465,500.00. Every line rolls forward. The other entry is not depreciation: March 16, 2026, “Proceeds from the crawler crane sale, paid to Cinderbrook Bank against the term loan, cred”. It leaves EQ-2740 with a net book value of ($69,387.68), below nothing: followed up in stage 3.

trail.what: Read every invoice line against the policy: a repair is an expense
trail.result: One line is a repair, not equipment: Cascade Iron Equipment invoice CIE-26-30612, line 3, $41,250.00 for “Shop work order WO-6127: rebuild hydraulic pump and both final drives, excavator”. It rebuilt the pump and final drives of EQ-3388, an asset HGC already owned, and was capitalized as part of EQ-4416. Expensing it lowers the loader’s cost to $117,850.00 and its June depreciation by $441.96; income is overstated by $40,808.04 (CAP-01).

trail.what: Recompute every asset’s FY2026 depreciation from the policy
trail.result: Every asset’s depreciation recomputes to the cent at its register life and the policy’s salvage: $424,700.00, account 6600. The month placed in service counts in full; assets that reached the end of their life in the year take only what was left.

trail.what: Compare every register life with the policy’s class life
trail.result: One register life differs from the policy: EQ-3388, hydraulic excavator, 45-ton (bought used), is depreciated over 60 months; the policy’s life for heavy earthmoving equipment is 120, with no documented shorter life. On the register it was fully depreciated by December 2024. At the policy life FY2026 depreciation is $23,343.96 ($1,945.33 a month) and accumulated depreciation at June 30, 2026 is $151,735.74, not $233,440.00: overstated by $81,704.26 (DEP-01).

One worked no hours in April to June: EQ-2740, “Sold March 16, 2026 to Brightwater Crane & Rigging LLC”, which confirms SALE-01. 4 fully depreciated assets are still in daily use (EQ-3122, EQ-3388, EQ-3901, EQ-3990): a sign the lives may be short for this fleet, for the CPA to weigh (LIFE-01).

trail.what: Depreciation and Use
trail.result: Depreciation recomputes to $424,700 · EQ-3388 life 60 against 120 · EQ-2740 idle since its sale

trail.result: Read Westgate crane rental agreement WER-RA-3318.pdf: agreement WER-RA-3318, 36 months from September 1, 2025, $21,500.00 a month.

trail.result: Read Harbor Ridge office lease first amendment.pdf: a new 60-month term from January 1, 2026, rent from $32,000.00 a month rising 3% a year.

trail.what: Reading FY2026 lease schedule.xlsx
trail.result: Read FY2026 lease schedule.xlsx: the controller’s lease schedule for the notes, $1,484,173.90 disclosed.

trail.what: Read every rental under ASC 842: a lease, and if so, short-term or not
trail.result: Account 5400, $1,524,450.00, is the rental register’s $1,096,287.50 plus fuel and repairs. 4 rentals are tickets of under a month or run month to month or for no more than 12 months: short-term, rightly expensed. One is not: agreement WER-RA-3318 with Westgate Equipment Rentals rents one identified crane (serial named, no substitution) for 36 months, non-cancellable, used as HGC directs. It is a lease, expensed as a rental at $215,000.00 this year (LEASE-02).

trail.what: Classify the crane lease and measure it
trail.result: No purchase option and no transfer; 36 months is a small part of a crawler crane’s life, and the payments’ present value at 7.10%, $699,392.72, is 51.8% of the crane’s $1,350,000.00 value: an operating lease. At June 30, 2026, after 10 payments, the lease liability and the right-of-use asset are $519,770.65. The rent is level, so the year’s expense is right; the balance sheet is missing both (LEASE-02).

trail.what: Measure the office lease and compare the controller’s schedule
trail.result: The office lease’s new term, January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2030, is an operating lease that is not recognized. Its rent rises 3% each January, $32,000.00 to $36,016.28 a month. At June 30, 2026 the lease liability is $1,580,613.31 and the right-of-use asset $1,568,742.50. The controller’s schedule used $32,000.00 for all 54 months left and disclosed $1,484,173.90, $96,439.41 short. Straight-line, January to June cost $203,870.81, not the $192,000.00 paid: rent is understated by $11,870.81 (LEASE-01).
trail.source: Harbor Ridge office lease first amendment.pdf

trail.what: Test the Leases
trail.result: One rental is a lease, $519,771 · the office lease $1,580,613, disclosed $96,439 short · rent understated $11,871

trail.what: Set what was found against materiality
trail.result: In income the known misstatements nearly offset: the $69,387.68 unrecorded gain against $40,808.04 of capitalized repair, $23,343.96 of depreciation and $11,870.81 of rent, a net ($6,635.13). The balance sheet is another matter: $2,100,383.96 of lease liabilities is missing, 618% of materiality, and the sold crane overstates cost by $553,061.60. The FY2026 covenant procedures read the lease note’s $1,484,173.90 (their DEF-01); this audit finds $2,100,383.96. The CPA weighs these with the other FY2026 areas. The machine stops here.

checks.title: Roll cost and accumulated depreciation forward, asset by asset

EQ-4415, the gps machine control and layout system bought June 8, 2026 for $84,150.00, has no request at all (APR-01).

checks.title: Test both disposals against their documents and the register
checks.detail: EQ-3205 was scrapped on February 20, 2026 for no proceeds: fully depreciated, removed at $102,600.00 of cost and accumulated depreciation, no gain or loss.
